title: The Command That Arrived Twice: Retrying What Was Not Acknowledged, and Applying It Once

questions.question: The acknowledgement of a command is lost. What does the sender do?
questions.explanation: It cannot tell the command was lost from the answer. The first acknowledgement of 10 commands lost was 20 arrivals.

questions.question: A command arrives a second time. What must the receiver do?
options: Not apply it, and acknowledge it
questions.explanation: It applied each once and refused 10 duplicates.

questions.question: Why does the receiver acknowledge a duplicate?
options: The first acknowledgement was lost, and without another the sender retries until it fails
questions.explanation: The acknowledgement is how the sender stops.

questions.question: A command has been sent 5 times, its limit, and is due again. What happens?
options: It fails, is removed from the waiting commands, and is listed
questions.explanation: The command was transmitted 5 times and then failed.

questions.question: Sequence numbers are 16 bits. What happens at 65536?
questions.explanation: 70000 commands used 65536 numbers with none twice in a row. The last of 70000 was 4463.

questions.question: A receiver remembers the last two numbers. What happens to a retry of an old command?
options: It is applied twice at once
questions.explanation: It has fallen out of the window. Number 1 was accepted again after two others.
